# Judge's ruling on rung I (`rung-int-semantics-walk`): the held `shift` declaration

Invoked on the worker's partial stop at `f37f060f1`. I read the net change (`git diff abdfbb2db...HEAD`), the four milestones, `REPORT.md`, `record.md`, the probe captures under `probes/`, the specification passages both cite (with their surroundings), the precedents at the cited lines, and the batch record `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md`. I ran nothing but `git apply --check` on the trial patch. No skeptic had run before this ruling; every claim judged below is the worker's.

## 1. The stop, as reported

Everything in the brief landed and passes except one item: declaring the specification's `shift(self, k): ZZ` on `trait ZZ` of `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi`. The worker measured that the declaration makes every `walk` run fail at static analysis with `Variable shift is already declared.` on the library's own parameters and one local named `shift` (`probes/shift-collision-layer1.txt` to `layer4.txt`: `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2080-2083` and `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3668-3671` and `:3686-3687` at the base tree's numbering, which the captures print one and two lines lower because the trial's inserted declaration and body precede them; `Library/RangeInternals.fsi:194-195`, `:263-264`, `:323-324`, `:431-432`; thirty sites in `Library/RangeInternals.fss`; and `Library/List.fss:311`), measured the whole repair as a trial (`probes/route-i-trial-patch.txt`: the declaration plus every rename; under it the full test with its six `shift` assertions printed `PASS`, `tests/subArray.fss` exited 0, `probes/route-i-trial-run.txt`; the checker count stayed 103, `probes/checker-count-route-i-trial.txt`), reverted it, and held the item for Pavol with four options (`REPORT.md` section 5), parking the six assertions in `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXShiftRungI.fss`.

## 2. Is this one of the reserved forks? No.

The forks that reach Pavol are `explorations/coordinator/PLAN.md:52` (the array representation; the library route; any change of semantics against the spec; deleting a test to get green) and the two the batch record adds for this rung (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md`, section I, last paragraph: a change to the type of an existing declaration; a catchable throw that would change how the interpreter maps Java exceptions in general), plus the shared prefix's "a renamed or removed declaration a gated test uses". Against the trial patch:

- The array representation and the library route are not touched. The batch record itself places the declaration in this one library and no other (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md`, section B, "the spec's `shift` is declared only in the one library, by rung I").
- It is not a change of semantics against the specification; it is the specification's own declaration (`Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:695-702`) and Pavol's decision of 2026-09-22 as quoted at `CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md:18` ("the spec's spelling `shift` declared on ℤ beside it"). The renames change no semantics: `shift: I` at `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2080-2083` is a positional parameter without a default, not a keyword-parameter declaration (the distinct kind at `Specification/basic/declarations.tex:243-244`), so no call site names it, and none does (section 4 below).
- No test is deleted (section 6, step 2, on the `XXX` file).
- No existing declaration changes type: the patch adds one functional method to `trait ZZ`, which is what the brief instructed (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md`, section I, "(a) The spec's `shift`, declared"), and renames parameters, which are declarations of a kind no gated test uses. The declarations gated tests do use, `shiftLeft`, `shiftRight`, `<<` and `>>` on `Range`, keep their names and types.
- The catchable throw is settled and measured (`REPORT.md` section 4.1); it is not at issue.

So the stop is not a reserved fork. The brief's own stop was narrower than the worker read it: "the library's other `shift` is the array-origin dotted method (`.fsi:1293`, `:1316`, `:1336`, `:1416`, `:1446`), and a collision with it is a stop" (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md`, section I). The measured collision is not with the dotted method; the trial showed the dotted method does not collide (`tests/subArray.fss`, the corpus's one caller of an array's `.shift(`, exited 0 under the trial, `probes/route-i-trial-run.txt`), which is what `Specification/basic/declarations.tex:416-425` predicts: a name immediately after the `.` of a dotted method invocation is exempt from the scope rule.

## 3. What the specification settles, and how

It settles the item twice over, and in the direction of the trial patch.

1. **`shift` is a functional method of ℤ.** `Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:695-702`: `shift(self, k: IndexInt): ZZ`, "The result of `shift(x,k)` is ⌊x·2^k⌋ … positive values of k shifts the bits to the left, and negative values of k shifts the bits to the right." The explicit `self` makes it a functional method, called `shift(x, k)`, not `x.shift(k)`; the team's own dormant draft has it in exactly this form beside `even` and `odd` (`Library/incomplete/basic/Fortress.Number.fsi:162`, `:172-173`). Option 2 of `REPORT.md` section 5 (a dotted method) and option 3 (another spelling) are therefore against the specification's form, and option 4 (leave it undeclared) is against Pavol's decision. The option set had one member consistent with both, and it is the trial.

2. **A parameter named `shift` in the library is then a static error, so the parameters must be renamed.** `Specification/basic/declarations.tex:426-431`: "It is also a static error for multiple declarations with overlapping reaches to declare the same name in the same namespace unless the declarations are overloaded or one declaration shadows the other." `:435-436`: "The reach of a functional method declaration is the component containing that declaration", which for `shift` on `ZZ` is `FortressLibrary`, the component that also holds `trait Range`'s `shiftLeft(shift: I)` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3668-3671`). `:459-461` gives a parameter its own reach inside that component, so the reaches overlap. The list of permitted shadowing at `:476-529` admits a keyword parameter (`:508-511`), `self` and `result`, and fields or dotted methods; a positional parameter is not on it, and `:533` closes the list: "No other shadowing is permitted in a Fortress program." A variable and a function are not overloaded. So within `FortressLibrary` alone the collision is a static error under the specification, independent of the implementation. For the importing components (`RangeInternals`, `List`, and every program) `:454-456` gives an imported declaration the reach of the importing component, which is the reading the shared implementation enforces (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/disambiguator/ExprDisambiguator.scala:745-763`, `checkForShadowingVar`, which rejects a variable whose name is any variable or function in scope). The worker's `probes/ShadowEven.fss` shows the same rule already in force for `even` and `numerator` (`probes/ShadowEven.txt`), two of the five functional methods `trait ZZ` declares today (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:539-543`).

Rule 4 of the shared prefix says a divergence is settled by the specification; here both the declaration and its consequence are settled, and the worker's own report cites the settling passages (`REPORT.md` section 5, second paragraph). What the worker took to Pavol as "a decision for Pavol" (that `shift` becomes a name no program may bind under `walk`) is the specification's rule at `:454-456` and `:533` applied to a name the specification itself declares. It is the language as written, and it is the same condition `even`, `odd`, `numerator`, `narrow` and `widen` are under today.

## 4. Where the specification is silent, and what I decided under the silence

- **The count's type.** The spec's `IndexInt` names no type in the library (`grep -rnw IndexInt Library/*.fs[si] ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/*.fs[si]` matches nothing). The brief settles this: `AnyIntegral`, `LSHIFT`'s own type (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:637`), "unless the rung argues another". The trial uses `AnyIntegral`. Decided: keep it.
- **The replacement name.** The trial renames every colliding parameter and the `List.fss` local to `amount`. It is measured clean (the trial's `PASS`, `subArray`, checker 103). Decided: keep `amount`; another name would need the measurement again for nothing.
- **The reserved-name consequence, measured.** `grep -rnw shift` over every `.fss` and `.fsi` outside `Library/` and `Specification/` (explorations, `ProjectFortress/tests`, `library_tests`, `compiler_tests`, `demos`, `LibraryBuiltin`) finds `shift` bound as a parameter or local nowhere: every hit is a comment, a string or a dotted `.shift(` call. The one other `shiftLeft(shift: I)` is in the top-level `CompilerLibrary/` directory (`CompilerLibrary/FortressLibrary.fsi:2061-2064`), which is on no source path and in no build file (`explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md:194`, `:207`). So the cost to the corpus is zero files. The compiled path is untouched (no prelude declaration, `CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md`, section B), so a compiled program may still bind `shift` where a `walk` program may not; that asymmetry already exists for every functional-method name of the interpreter's library and is not new in kind. This is reported to Pavol below.
- **The home of the six `shift` assertions.** They were first written in `ProjectFortress/tests/IntSemanticsRungI.fss:94-99` (commit `cf01b652d`), where the brief put them ("The test, first": `shift(3, 33)`, `shift(3, -1)`, `shift(-3, -1)`), and their recorded failure is `test-before.txt` (`Variable shift is not defined.`, six times, exit 255). They moved to `XXXShiftRungI.fss` only because the item was held. With the hold lifted they go back: home 1, "the cheapest form is an extra assert in the .fss file the rung already added" (shared prefix). The `XXX` file is then removed from the branch. This is not the "deleting a test to get green" fork of `PLAN.md:52`: the file has never been on `main`, it was the placeholder for a deferral that has ended, and its assertions land in the gated test and pass. The alternative, renaming it to a plain `ShiftRungI.fss` and landing two files, was considered; it would make `testSystem` 395 where the gate expects 394 (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md`, section 3, "testSystem rises 393 -> 394 by the shards' sum") for no gain in coverage. Decided: fold and remove. The capture of the `XXX` file going red on the deliberate fix (`probes/harness-XXXShiftRungI-deliberate-fix.txt`) stays committed as the record of the deferral while it lasted.

## 5. The worker's claims, right and wrong

Right, by citation:
- The collision is real and its five layers are measured exactly (`probes/shift-collision-layer1.txt` to `layer5.txt`; I confirmed the sites at `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2080-2083`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3668-3671`, `:3686-3687`, `Library/RangeInternals.fsi:194-195`, `Library/List.fss:311`).
- The cause is the disambiguator's no-shadowing check (`ExprDisambiguator.scala:745-763`) and the specification's rule (`declarations.tex:426-432`, `:435-436`, `:533`); both citations hold when read with their surroundings.
- The repair was measured whole before it was held: `probes/route-i-trial-patch.txt` applies cleanly to `f37f060f1` (`git apply --check`, this ruling) and covers every site the layers found; its effect is captured (`probes/route-i-trial-run.txt`, `probes/checker-count-route-i-trial.txt`, `probes/harness-XXXShiftRungI-deliberate-fix.txt`).
- The dotted array-origin `shift` does not collide (`subArray` under the trial), and the `XXX` mechanism was shown to work (`FileTests.java:346-361`, `:384-403`, read; the capture shows `Missing expected failure`).
- Everything else in the brief is landed, measured and asserted; I read the natives' diff and find the shapes sound: the count comparison precedes the negation in all four fixed widths; `Int.shiftCount` (`Int.java:261-272`) reads an `FNN64` of `2^63` or more as beyond every width and an `FBigNum` exactly or clamped; `Int.lcm` (`Int.java:274-284`) tests the two magnitudes without a `long` before `Math.abs`, then `multiplyExact`; `BigNum.shiftLeft` (`BigNum.java:237-250`) maps a right shift of `2^31` or more to `0`/`-1`, which is exact since a `BigInteger` has fewer than `2^31` bits; `toB`'s `FNN64` branch (`BigNum.java:46-48`) is `makeZZfromNN64`'s spelling (`simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.java:117-119`).

Wrong, by citation:
- Reading the brief's stop as "a collision of the new name". The brief's sentence names the array-origin dotted method as the thing a collision with which is a stop (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md`, section I, "(a) The spec's `shift`, declared"); the measured collision is with parameter names, and the dotted method was shown not to collide.
- Treating the reserved name as a language decision that needs Pavol. It is the specification's rule (`declarations.tex:454-456`, `:533`) already in force for every functional-method name of the library, as the worker's own `probes/ShadowEven.txt` shows, applied to a declaration the specification makes (`basic-integers.tex:696`) and Pavol has already decided (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md:18`).
- Counting the three unlisted files as a reason to stop. `PLAN.md:52`: "Any source in the tree may be edited under the rule above; which file it is in is not a decision." Batch rule 1 is what matters, and it holds: rung B edits `nativeHelpers/simpleIntArith.java`, `simpleLongArith.java`, `LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss`, `library_tests/IntConversionsRungW.fss` and its compiler tests (shared prefix, "The batch manifest"); none of `RangeInternals.fss`, `RangeInternals.fsi` or `List.fss` is among them, so the gather stays clean.
- Offering options 2, 3 and 4 as open. Each is against either the specification's form (`basic-integers.tex:696`, a functional method) or Pavol's decision; only option 1 is consistent with both (section 3 above).

The worker's judgement to measure the whole trial before holding, and to put the assertions where the harness would notice a silent fix, was right and is what makes the repair round short.

## 6. Instructions for the repair worker

Work only in `/home/user/fortress-intsem-i`, on `wip/rung-int-semantics-walk`, with the shell set up as the shared prefix says. The Java natives are done and are not touched. No `ant compileAll` is needed (no `.java` changes); no `ant testFast` or `ant testSystem`.

Then confirm no bound `shift` remains in the library: `grep -rnw shift Library/*.fss Library/*.fsi ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/*.fss ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/*.fsi` must show only the array-origin dotted declarations and bodies (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1293`, `:1316`, `:1336`, `:1416`, `:1446` and their component sites), the new declaration in `trait ZZ` (`.fsi`, after `even(self): Boolean` at `:543`) and its body in the component (`.fss`, after `RSHIFT` at `:883-884`, bound to `BigNum$LShift`), and comments.

2. Move the six assertions of `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXShiftRungI.fss:14-19` into `ProjectFortress/tests/IntSemanticsRungI.fss` directly after line 96 (`assert(twoTo63 + bigZero, ...)`), unchanged; every name they use is already bound there (`three` :15, `minusThree` :20, `minL` :27, `threeL` :46, `twoTo63` :73, `bigThree` :78, `bigMinusThree` :79). Then `git rm ProjectFortress/tests/XXXShiftRungI.fss`. The test's recorded failure for these assertions is already `test-before.txt` (the first version, `cf01b652d`, had them at `:94-99`).

3. Run the test as the trial was run and re-capture `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-walk/test-after.txt` (`PASS`, `exit=0`). If the library edit seems to have no effect, the interpreter's caches under `default_repository/caches/` are stale (`CLAUDE.md`); the harness script below uses a fresh caches directory by construction.

Re-run the 37-file regression subset of `probes/harness-regression-2.txt` (without `XXXShiftRungI.fss` if it was in the list) and capture `probes/harness-regression-3.txt`: `OK (37 tests)`. ## 7. An observation for the record, not for repair

The trial patch preserves, as it should, three 2012 defects in the bodies it renames: `Library/RangeInternals.fss:663` and `:667` (`LeftRange3D.shiftLeft`/`shiftRight` write `l_k-shift` and `l_k+shift` where `shift` is the tuple `(I, J, K)` bound at `:661`/`:665` and `shift_k` was meant), `:783` and `:787` (`RightRange3D`, `r_k-shift`, `r_k+shift`) and `:1355` and `:1359` (`StridedFullRange2D`, `r_i-shift, r_j-shift` and `r_i+shift, r_j+shift` for `shift_i`, `shift_j`). ## 8. What reaches Pavol, out of the loop

- I ruled that declaring the specification's `shift` on ℤ, with the library's own parameters named `shift` renamed, is the specification's settled answer and not a fork. # Judge's second ruling on rung I: the skeptic's refusal at `ecc71113a`

Invoked on the skeptic's refusal of the landed rung (`SKEPTIC.md`, commit `ecc71113a`). I read the net change (`git diff abdfbb2db...HEAD`), the eight milestones, `REPORT.md`, `record.md`, `SKEPTIC.md`, the skeptic's captures under `probes/skeptic/`, the batch record `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md`, the specification passages both cite with ten lines either side, and the natives and library declarations at the cited lines. I ran nothing. The worktree was clean.

The first ruling above (lines 1-87) is left byte for byte as it was, because `REPORT.md`, `record.md` and `SKEPTIC.md` cite it by section and by line; one error in it is corrected here and not edited in: line 14 cites `CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md:18` for Pavol's decision, and that line is blank; the decision is `:17` (section 5 below). Line numbers of this part start at 89.

**Decision: repair.** The skeptic's refusal ground stands, and so do its findings 2 to 8, each by the citations below. The repair round edits one Java file (`BigNum.java`, two sites), adds three assertions to the gated test, and rewrites the parts of `REPORT.md` and `record.md` the findings touch; it opens four ledger rows on the skeptic's measurements. The Java natives of the four fixed widths, the library declaration and the renames are not touched.

## 1. Finding 1, the refusal ground: upheld

**What is true.** `BigNum.shiftLeft` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/BigNum.java:237-250`) bounds the count at `:243` (`if (v > Integer.MAX_VALUE) throw Int.overflow();`) and then calls `u.shiftLeft((int) v)` inside a `try` at `:244-249`, translating the `ArithmeticException`. The JVM's `BigInteger.shiftLeft` allocates the shifted magnitude before its range check throws, so for `3 << 2147483647` about 268 MB is asked for first. The interpreter's launcher gives the JVM `-Xmx256m` unless `JAVA_FLAGS` is set (`bin/fortress:28-29`), and the harness gives it 768 MB (root `build.xml:131`, `junitMem`, used by the `junit` task's `maxmemory` at `:1181`; `probes/harness-one.sh` copies that as `-Xmx768m`). Measured by the skeptic on the landed tree: under `bin/fortress` with `JAVA_FLAGS` unset the gated test dies at `IntSemanticsRungI.fss:93` with `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space` (`probes/skeptic/test-default-heap.txt:1-3`), and prints `PASS` without that line (`probes/skeptic/test-default-heap-no93.txt`); the same shift is `THROWS IntegerOverflow` at 768m and 4g (`probes/skeptic/SkBigAlloc.txt:6-10`) and an `OutOfMemoryError` at 256m (`:1-4`).

**Why it is refusal-grade.** Three reasons, any one enough. `record.md` FACTS line 2 (`record.md:10`) and `REPORT.md` section 4.4 (`REPORT.md:71-73`) claim an unrepresentable left shift raises "a catchable `IntegerOverflow`", unconditionally; it does so only above the launcher's heap, and a claim that holds only under the shared prefix's `JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g ..."` is not a fact about the tree. An `OutOfMemoryError` is a `java.lang.Error` that no Fortress `catch` and no harness expected-failure sees, so the gated assertion `:93` is a red at the tree's own default that the gate cannot show. And a runtime that allocates 268 MB to learn that a shift does not fit, when the answer is one `bitLength()`, is the wrong shape for a language whose specification says overflow "throws an `IntegerOverflow`" (`Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:154-155`, read with `:140-170`).

**The repair, and why it is exact.** The skeptic's one line after `:243`, `if (u.abs().bitLength() + v > Integer.MAX_VALUE) throw Int.overflow();`, trialled in a scratch overlay (`probes/skeptic/fix-trial-patch.txt`), makes the unmodified test print `PASS` at `-Xmx256m` (`probes/skeptic/fix-trial-default-heap.txt`). It is exact by the worker's own measurement in `REPORT.md:71`: `3 << 2147483645` succeeds with bit length 2147483647 and `3 << 2147483646` throws, which is `2 + 2147483645 <= Integer.MAX_VALUE < 2 + 2147483646`; the JVM's limit is a magnitude of `Integer.MAX_VALUE` bits, and `u.abs().bitLength()` is the magnitude's bit length (for a negative power of two, `u.bitLength()` alone is one less, so `abs()` is not decoration). Two things the repair worker must keep:

- `:243` stays, and stays first. `Int.shiftCount` (`Int.java:261-272`) clamps an `NN64` count of `2^63` or more and a `ZZ` count beyond a `long` to `Long.MAX_VALUE`; without `:243` ahead of it, `bitLength + v` overflows the `long`, the precheck falls through, and `(int) v` is `-1`, a silent right shift. The existing assertion `IntSemanticsRungI.fss:95` (`bigThree LSHIFT twoTo63` overflows) is the guard on that order.
- The `try`/`catch` at `:244-249` stays as a backstop. The precheck's exactness rests on a JDK-internal constant (`BigInteger.MAX_MAG_LENGTH`), which is the JDK's to change; the catch costs nothing and keeps the translation if the constant ever moves.

**What the worker got wrong here, and what right.** `REPORT.md:73` took a decision, "translating the JVM's own check rather than predicting it keeps the limit the JVM's", without measuring at the launcher's heap; the shared prefix's `JAVA_FLAGS` hid the failure, and the base tree fails the same way (the base's `u.shiftLeft((int) v)` at base `BigNum.java:224` is the same call), so this is not a regression but it is the rung's claim. Everything else in section 4.4 is right and stays: the negative count of any size, zero shifted, the count beyond `Integer.MAX_VALUE`, and the choice of `IntegerOverflow` (`opr-overview.tex:154-155`).

## 2. Finding 2, the unbounded `ZZ`'s `LCM`: upheld; home 1

**What the specification settles.** `Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:520-521` declare `GCD` and `LCM` on ℤ itself (the rendered `\Method` lines, `opr LCM(self, other: ZZ): ZZ`), and `:527-529` say of `LCM`: "The result is always nonnegative. If either argment is 1, the result equals the other argument. If either argument is 0, the result is 0." So the unbounded `ZZ` is squarely inside the clause, not beside it. `BigNum$Lcm` (`BigNum.java:176-188`, bound as `ZZ`'s `LCM` at `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:871-872`) computes `u.divide(g).multiply(v)` with `g = u.gcd(v)`, carrying `v`'s sign, and divides by `g = 0` when both are zero: measured, `1 LCM -5` is `-5`, `-4 LCM 6` is `-12`, and `0 LCM 0` ends the run with `ArithmeticException: BigInteger divide by zero` (`probes/skeptic/SkBigLcm.walk.txt:1-4`, `:8-9`). `BigNum$Gcd` (`:170-174`) is `u.gcd(v)`, which the JVM defines nonnegative, and the capture agrees (`:6`, `0 GCD -4 = 4`).

**Whether it is this rung's.** Yes. The batch record's (b) names `Int$Gcd`/`Int$Lcm` and `Long$Gcd`/`Long$Lcm` and puts only the unsigned pair out (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md:47`, "The unsigned `GCD`/`LCM` have their own helper ... and are out"); it does not put the `BigNum` one out, and rule 2 of the shared prefix says a repaired defect is evidence of the same defect elsewhere in that file, which this is: `BigNum.java` is a file the rung edits, and `REPORT.md:128`'s count ("sat in three natives; two are fixed here, and the third is ... dormant") missed the reachable fourth. Neither of the rung's two stops applies (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md:57`): no declaration changes type, and `BigInteger` has no overflow to raise, so nothing touches how Java exceptions are mapped.

**Decision: home 1, repaired here.** The alternative the skeptic offered, home 2 (an `XXX` file, row 334 left open for ℤ), is rejected: the fix is four lines in the shape of the precedent the rung already cites for `Int.lcm` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:616-619`: zero first, then `|u / g| * |v|`), and a deferral would cost a file, a `.test`, a deliberate-red capture and a half-closed row for no measurement gained. The shape: if either argument is zero, return `BigInteger.ZERO`; otherwise take both magnitudes with `abs()` before the existing `gcd`, the smaller-first swap (`:179-186`, which compares signed values today and is only right on magnitudes) and the divide-multiply. This is also a third instance of row 336's shape closed by the rung (a raw `ArithmeticException` from a division by zero, `record.md:36`), so the row 336 note must say `0 LCM 0` is `0` on `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` and `ZZ`, not "on both widths".

## 3. Finding 3, a `ZZ32` receiver with a `ZZ`, `NN32` or `NN64` count: upheld as home 3; the fix is reserved and reaches Pavol

**What is true.** `ZZ32`'s own pair is declared `opr LSHIFT(self,b:ZZ64):ZZ32` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:688-691`; api `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:491-492`), `ZZ64`'s component pair `opr LSHIFT(self,b:AnyIntegral):ZZ64` (`.fss:756-759`; its api line says `b:ZZ64`, `.fsi:530-531`, a second api/component mismatch of the kind row 345 records), and `Integral[\I\]` promises `opr LSHIFT(self,b:AnyIntegral):I` (`.fss:637-638`, `.fsi:431-432`). `ZZ32` extends `ZZ64` (`.fss:646`), so a count that is not a `ZZ64` misses `ZZ32`'s pair and lands on `ZZ64`'s, computed by `Long$LShift` at width 64 and returned as a `ZZ64`: `3 LSHIFT big(widen(33))` is `25769803776 : ZZ64`, `3 LSHIFT unsigned(33)` and `3 LSHIFT unsigned(widen(33))` the same, where a `ZZ64` count of 33 gives `0 : ZZ32` (`probes/skeptic/SkWalkOnly.walk.txt:2-6`, `:9`; `probes/skeptic/sk-base-cases.txt`). The `NN` counts gave this answer on the base tree; the `ZZ` count ended the run with `ProgramError: Value 33 might not fit in ZZ64.` until rung I's `Int.shiftCount` (`sk-base-cases.txt:3-10` against `:1-2`). So section 6.1 of `REPORT.md` turned a loud failure into a quiet value it does not state, and its home-1 assertion `IntSemanticsRungI.fss:82` (`-3 RSHIFT big(widen(40))` = -1) is the same at either width and tests nothing of this.

**What the specification says.** Nothing on `LSHIFT`/`RSHIFT`: the worker's grep over `Specification/basic` and `Specification/basic-lib` matches nothing (`REPORT.md:4`), and I found no passage either. The receiver-width rule is Pavol's (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md:17`) and the library's own contract (`.fss:637-638`), not the specification's. So the outcome of rule 4 is a silent specification, and the home is 3: the skeptic's probes are committed, and a ledger row is opened (section 6).

**Why this rung does not repair it, and what I put to Pavol.** The clean fix is one declaration's type: `ZZ32`'s pair from `b:ZZ64` to `b:AnyIntegral` in `.fsi:491-492` and `.fss:688-691`, bound as now to `Int$LShift`/`$RShift`, which already read any count through `Int.shiftCount`. That is "a fix [that] would change the type of an existing declaration", the stop the batch record reserves for this rung (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md:57`), so it is not done here. Candidates and costs, for Pavol: (a) the type change above, two files, one declaration, no assertion of the shared table moves (its `ZZ64`-count cases `IntSemanticsRungI.fss:42-44` still reach `ZZ32`'s pair), the checker-count stage possibly moved since it reads `Library/`; (b) an added overload `opr LSHIFT(self,b:AnyIntegral):ZZ32` beside the `b:ZZ64` one, which adds rather than changes a declaration and so passes the stop's letter, rejected as evasive and as leaving a redundant narrower pair; (c) leave it, which is the state after this rung. My recommendation is (a), after the batch.

## 4. Finding 4, the off-by-one citations: upheld

Verified with `grep -n` on the batch record: `:17` is "(a) Row 335", `:18` blank; `:35` "The siblings", `:36` blank; `:45` "(a) The spec's `shift`, declared", `:46` blank; `:57` "What it closes, and where it stops", `:58` blank; section I runs `:39-57`. The worker's `:18` at `REPORT.md:4` is copied from line 14 of the first ruling, which is mine to own; `:36`, `:46` and `:58` at `REPORT.md:55`, `:81`, `:122` and "lines 40-58" at `:11` are the worker's.

## 5. Finding 5, the GCD/LCM passage: upheld, with the reconciling reading added

`basic-integers.tex:523-525`: "The result is always nonnegative. If either argment is 0, the result equals the other argument." and `:527-529` the same for `LCM` with 1. Read alone, the second sentence gives `0 GCD -4 = -4`; the first forbids it. The reconciliation is in the source two lines above the rendered declarations: the chapter's own commented declarations at `:518-519` are `opr GCD(self, other: ZZ): NN` and `opr LCM(self, other: ZZ): NN`, a return type of ℕ, under which "equals the other argument" can only mean its magnitude. So the nonnegative reading is the specification's, with the return type as the evidence, and Pavol's row-334 decision (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md:19`) confirms it. `REPORT.md`'s `spec:` line and section 4.2 say this in one sentence each.

## 6. Findings 6, 7 and 8: outside the rung, each measured, each gets a row

Rule: every defect measured in this rung has one of three homes, and a defect the specification settles whose repair lies outside the rung lands with a verified ledger row (shared prefix, the fourth case). The skeptic measured all three with committed probes; `record.md`'s "Rung I opens no row" is replaced. Provisional numbers follow the batch record (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md:73`: from 378, B's siblings row first, the gather assigning final numbers in manifest order): finding 3 is 379, finding 6 is 380, finding 7 is 381, finding 8 is 382.

The specification is silent; home 3; row 380 as the skeptic wrote it. Rung B does not change a 64-bit shift of 3 by 33, so it persists after the batch.
- **Finding 7** (`longOverflowingMul`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleLongArith.java:70-85`, tests `Long.MAX_VALUE / Math.abs(a) < Math.abs(b)` at `:82`, the positive bound, so a product equal to `Long.MIN_VALUE` throws; through `REM` at `CompilerBuiltin.fss:597`, `MIN REM 2`, `MIN MOD 2`, `MIN GCD 2` and `2 GCD MIN` throw where `walk` gives `0`, `0`, `2`, `2`; `probes/skeptic/SkMulMin.compiled.txt:2-7`, `SkMulMin.walk.txt:1-6`): the specification settles it (`opr-overview.tex:154-155`, overflow only when the result does not fit; `basic-integers.tex:523-525`, `GCD` nonnegative). The fix is in rung B's file; row 381 as the skeptic wrote it, with one sentence added: if rung B's siblings rider took `Math.multiplyExact` (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md:35`, its last clause), this row closes in the same landing, which the coordinator checks at the gather.
- **Finding 8** (`shift(3, 33)` is `Variable shift is not defined.` compiled and `25769803776` under `walk`; `shift` bindable as a local or parameter compiled and `Variable shift is already declared.` under `walk`; `probes/skeptic/SkShiftCall.*.txt`, `SkShiftLocal.*.txt`, `SkShiftParam.*.txt`): the specification settles both `walk`'s way (`basic-integers.tex:696`; `Specification/basic/declarations.tex:454-456`, `:533`), the repair is a compiler prelude declaration reserved by the batch (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md:29`, "No declaration goes into the compiler prelude"), and the ledger already has this kind of row: 344, "the compiler prelude declares none of the three locality functions the specification names" (`explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:355`, kind "prelude gap"). The skeptic's row for finding 3 (379) is home 3 by section 3, with the api/component mismatch at `.fsi:530-531` added to its text.

## 7. The two parties' claims, right and wrong

The worker, right: everything the first ruling found right stands, and the repair round executed the first ruling faithfully; its three departures (36 not 37 files, `probes/harness-regression-2.txt:22`; seven not five dotted declarations, `.fsi:1557` and `:1688`; the red captured before the patch, `test-before-shift.txt`) were each settled by a primary source and were right. # Rung C: coercion in the interpreter

problem: under `walk`, a value that its declared type's own `coerce` accepts is refused at a function's parameter, at an overloaded call and at a typed binding; re-measured on `47437c65f`: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-interp-coercion/probes/red-before.txt:3`, `:20`, `:39`, `:56`, `:98`, `:117`, `:137`
spec: where coercion happens, `Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:98-110`; only when no declaration applies without one, then the most specific, `:455-460` and `:516-536`; the specificity relation, `:469-484`; receivers of dotted methods are not coerced, `:431-436`; coercions do not chain, `:127-132`; the converted call is an ordinary call dispatched at run time, `:253-265` with `Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:73-78`, `:466-468` (section 4); tuples convert element by element, `:694-705`
precedent: the team's "TODO add checks for COERCE, right here." (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/OverloadedFunction.java:792` at `47437c65f`); the lookup of a trait's lifted functions at the top level of its environment, copied from `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/types/FTraitOrObjectOrGeneric.java:139-159`; the specificity relation, copied from `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/CoercionOracle.scala:71-83`; the ordinary dispatch path `OverloadedFunction.applyInnerPossiblyGeneric` and `OverloadedMethod.applyMethod`, which the converted arguments re-enter (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/OverloadedFunction.java:758-780`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/OverloadedMethod.java:55-65`)
deviation: the coercion is chosen on the run-time value, where the specification chooses it statically (`conversions-coercions.tex:567-570`; route A, `explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:92`), gated as `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXCoercionStaticRungC.fss` and `XXXCoercionStaticNarrowRungC.fss`; a call with no single most specific coercion is refused at the call, where the specification refuses the declarations (`Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:196-216`, `:247-273`); a coercion whose result is not of its type is refused at the call (`conversions-coercions.tex:184-186`); generic overloads are skipped by the coercion pass, and a generic trait's coercion is not instantiated from the target type (rows 388 and 389; `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/OverloadedFunction.java:826`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/Coercions.java:48-71`)
historical: under `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/`, `env/LazilyEvaluatedCell.java`, `evaluator/BaseEnv.java`, `evaluator/BuildEnvironments.java`, `evaluator/LHSEvaluator.java`, `evaluator/values/NonPrimitive.java`, `evaluator/values/OverloadedFunction.java` and `evaluator/values/OverloadedMethod.java`; and one new file in that tree, `evaluator/values/Coercions.java`; the rule that asks for this line is `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:246`

## 0. How this report was written

The subagent harness refused the worker's `.md` writes ("Subagents should return findings as text, not write report files"), in both of its rounds, and it refused the first skeptic's and the judge's. This report and `record.md` were composed at the gather of climb batch 4 from the worker's two structured results (run `wf_f54d0e4b-63d`, `rung:C` and `repair:C`), with the judge's ruling (`judge:C`, written out as `JUDGE.md`) and both skeptics' judgements (the second skeptic's `SKEPTIC.md` was written by it; the first judgement is appended to that file at the gather), as batch 3.5 did for its rung B (`explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-3.5/RECORD.md:13`). Where the first pass and the repair round differ, this report gives the landed state and says what the first pass did. Section 14 lists what the gather itself added.

## 1. What changed

`walk` applies the declared type's lifted `coerce_<T>`, found at the top level of the type's environment, in three kinds of place:
- a single function's, constructor's, method's, native's and varargs parameter (`NonPrimitive.typecheckParams` and `buildEnvFromParams`);
- an overloaded call where no overload applies without coercion: `OverloadedFunction.bestMatchWithCoercion`, called at the team's TODO, takes the most specific applicable coercion by `conversions-coercions.tex:469-484` and refuses an ambiguous call; the result is a `Coercions.CoercedCall`, kept in the per-argument-type cache, which converts the arguments and dispatches the converted arguments as an ordinary call through the owning `OverloadedFunction` (`Coercions.java:228-230`); an overloaded method converts and calls `applyMethod` again (`OverloadedMethod.java:56-63`);
- a typed local, top-level or field declaration, and an assignment to a typed variable or field (`LHSEvaluator`, `BaseEnv.assignValue`, `BuildEnvironments`, and `LazilyEvaluatedCell`, which carries the declared type and converts when first computed).

A declaration, parameter or assignment of tuple type converts element by element, an element already of its type kept (`Coercions.coerce` and `coerceTuple`, `Coercions.java:88-116`); a size mismatch, a varargs element or an element with no coercion stays the loud error it was.

Files: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/Coercions.java` (new, 271 lines); `OverloadedFunction.java` (`bestMatch`'s coercion pass, `bestMatchWithoutCoercion`, `bestMatchWithCoercion` with the ambiguity refusal); `OverloadedMethod.java`; `NonPrimitive.java`; `LHSEvaluator.java`; `BaseEnv.java`; `BuildEnvironments.java`; `env/LazilyEvaluatedCell.java`.

Tests, sixteen new `.fss` files, each with one comment line pointing at this report:
- home 1, `ProjectFortress/tests/`: `CoercionCallRungC`, `CoercionOverloadRungC`, `CoercionBindRungC`, `CoercionMostSpecificRungC`, `CoercionSpecTableRungC`, `CoercionRedispatchRungC`;
- home 2, `ProjectFortress/tests/`: `XXXCoercionStaticRungC`, `XXXCoercionStaticNarrowRungC`, `XXXCoercionReturnRungC`, `XXXCoercionGenericFnRungC`, `XXXCoercionGenericTraitRungC`, `XXXCoercionTupleOverloadRungC`;
- home 2, `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/`: `XXXCoercionAnyOverloadRungC` (with `CoercionAnyOverloadRungCLink.test` and `XXXCoercionAnyOverloadRungC.test`), `XXXCoercionGenericFnCompiledRungC` (`.test`), `XXXTupleLocalVarCompiledRungC` and `XXXTupleVarFieldCompiledRungC` (each with a `.test`, linked by `TupleVarCompiledRungCLink.test`).

33	## 10. The cost
34	
35	- **The caching holds for overloaded functions only.** `OverloadedFunction` keeps the coercions per argument types in its cache (`OverloadedFunction.java:760-776`) and re-dispatches every converted call. An overloaded method caches nothing, before the rung or after: `OverloadedMethod.mcache` is declared at `OverloadedMethod.java:28`, read at `:48` and `:56`, and written nowhere, so a converting overloaded method call runs `bestMatch` and the coercion pass on every call. The first pass's sentence "An overloaded call pays the cost once per argument types" held for overloaded functions only. The batch record's premise that overloaded methods share the per-argument-type cache through `OverloadedMethod.java:50` (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:65`, repeated at `:79`) is wrong for the same reason.
36	- **A single function's parameter is not cached**: each converting call looks up `coerce_<T>` and dispatches among its declarations; `bestMatchWithoutCoercion` does not use that function's cache, which could hold a `CoercedCall` and would then chain.
37	- **Pavol's question (5) of 2026-09-24** (`explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:82`): nothing happens in a class loader. The `coerce_` lookup runs only where a check fails, which today happens only on the way to an error; an overloaded function pays it once per argument types. One cost runs whether or not anything converts: every typed immutable top-level variable and every typed immutable field of every object instance evaluates its declared type when first forced (`BuildEnvironments.java:680-683`, `LazilyEvaluatedCell.java:66-68`, `Coercions.coerceToDeclared`, `Coercions.java:124-135`). Measured by the first skeptic, no difference above noise: base 2506, 2809 and 2733 ms against 2908, 2932 and 2572 ms, 400,000 instantiations with three typed fields at one thread (`probes/skeptic/fieldcost.txt`), on nproc 4, Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.80GHz, 2800.212 MHz, JDK 25, `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`, load 0.62 at the start (`probes/skeptic/fieldcost.txt:1`). # Rung N: sizes in the compiled type checker

problem: `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NatInferredChecker.fss:14` dies in the checker with `java.lang.Error: Not yet implemented` (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/junit-before.txt:4`), a written-out size with `ClassCastException: class com.sun.fortress.nodes.VarType cannot be cast to class com.sun.fortress.nodes.IntExpr` (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/junit-before.txt:185`), and the gate's checker-count stage meets the same crash on the array api (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/checker-count-before.txt:16`)
spec: `Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:68-90` (a `nat` or `int` parameter is instantiated with a number and may appear wherever a variable of type ℕ32 or ℤ32 can); for the return-type rule, `Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:95-103` with `:158-170` (static parameters identical up to α-equivalence and then ignored; the Subtype Rule compares return types); for the export checker's size comparison (`ExportChecker.equalIntExprs`), `Specification/basic/components/apis.tex:250-256` (a component's matching definition of an api declaration has the same header and type, `:256`)
precedent: the checker's operator track, the one of its two inference-variable tracks whose constraints are equalities only: `_InferenceVarOp` (`ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast:1593`), `OPrimitive` and `oEquivalent` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/Formula.scala:61`, `:805`), its reduce steps (`:355-371`) and its `makeSub` call (`:640-642`); the interpreter's rule `IntNat.unifyStaticArg` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/types/IntNat.java:126-146`); the kind-correct `STypesUtil.staticParamToArg` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/useful/STypesUtil.scala:333-345`); the shadow `explorations/perf-probes/nat/shadow.patch:1` with `explorations/perf-probes/nat/size-probes/keep-size-params.patch:1-22`
deviation: section 5 of this report, one line per difference from the shadow (under "Deviations from the shadow") and from the specification's spelling (under "Deviations from the specification's spelling"); `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/REPORT.md:87-99`
historical: `ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast`, the 30 regenerated files under `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes/` (26 changed, 4 new) and `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/nodes/FortressAst.scala`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/NodeFactory.java`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/exceptions/ApplicationError.scala`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/FnNameInfo.java`, and in `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/`: `typechecker/Formula.scala`, `typechecker/FormulaJUTest.scala`, `types/TypeAnalyzer.scala`, `types/TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala`, `useful/STypesUtil.scala`, `overloading/OverloadingOracle.scala`, `typechecker/AbstractMethodChecker.scala`, `typechecker/TypeWellFormedChecker.scala`, `typechecker/ExportChecker.scala`, `typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala`; the rule that asks for this line is `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:246`

## 1. What changed

The compiled type checker now checks `nat` and `int` static parameters, a size such as the `n` of `Vector[\RR64, n\]`, by the plan's minimal design: a size is a symbol or a literal, two sizes are equal when they are the same symbol or the same literal, an inference variable is bound by equality, and there is no arithmetic. A program with a size inferred from an argument, one with the size written out, and a method called on a sized receiver compile; a mismatch is refused; arithmetic in a size and inference of a `bool`, `dim` or `unit` parameter are refused with an error that names them. The checker-count stage reads 125 with the crash row `none`, the numbers the batch record predicted.

| file | what | code lines added |
|---|---|---|
| `astgen/Fortress.ast:1349-1353` | a node `_InferenceVarInt(Object id)` under `IntExpr`, beside `_InferenceVarType` (`:1061`) and `_InferenceVarOp` (`:1593`) | 1 (and its comment) |
| `nodes/` (30 files), `scala_src/nodes/FortressAst.scala` | regenerated from the node | generated |
| `nodes_util/NodeFactory.java:1182-1185` | `make_InferenceVarInt`, the twin of `make_InferenceVarOp` (`:1178-1180`) | 3 |
| `scala_src/typechecker/Formula.scala` | the size track: `NPrimitive` (`:66`), a third map in `And` and a third set in `Conjuncts` (`:50-51`, `:72-73`), `nEq` (`:100-105`), and a size case in each function that walks the two tracks: `and`, `imp` (`:205`), `reduce` (`:372-389`, `:425-433`), `solve`/`slv` (`:486-524`), `unify`, `getEquality`, `un` (`:643-646`, `:654-663`, `:687-693`), `cMap`, `eMap`, `neg`; `nEquivalent`/`nNotEquivalent` (`:808-812`) | 137 |
| `scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:331`, `:351-360`, `:807-808` | two `IntArg`s are equal by the rule above (the tree answered `pTrue()` for any two); `pEqv` on sizes, the twin of the op one (`:342-348`) | 12 |
| `scala_src/useful/STypesUtil.scala:550-568` | `makeInferenceArg`: a size gets an `_InferenceVarInt`; `bool`, `dim`, `unit` a named error in place of `NI.nyi()` | 20 |
| `STypesUtil.scala:801`, `:808-814`, `:1017`, `:1029` | `hasInferenceVars` finds an unsolved size; `hasSizeInferenceVars`; the size substitution reaches the recorded static arguments | (in the 20) |
| `scala_src/types/TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala:404-412`, `:484-488` | unification's size substitution carried through `reduceED`; `keep-size-params.patch`: `boundsSubstitution` keeps a `nat` or `int` parameter | 6 |
| `scala_src/overloading/OverloadingOracle.scala:90-106` | in the return-type rule, a size of the less specific declaration that the domains leave unsolved stays that declaration's own static parameter in the arrow checked against | 12 |
| `scala_src/typechecker/AbstractMethodChecker.scala:83-84` | the object's static parameters as kind-correct arguments (`staticParamsToArgs`) | 2 |
| `compiler/codegen/FnNameInfo.java:165-169` | `boundsFor` gives a size itself (`staticParamToArg`), not a `TypeArg` | 7 |
| `scala_src/typechecker/TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:41-48`, `:107-108`, `:144-145` | arithmetic in a size, in a type or in a static argument, refused with a named error | 10 |
| `scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala:247-249`, `exceptions/ApplicationError.scala:114` | a size left unknown in a call's static arguments is the "could not infer ... without context" error, and the message names the parameter | 2 |
| `scala_src/typechecker/ExportChecker.scala:645-646` | `equalIntExprs` compares sizes (`nEq`) instead of answering `false` | 1 |
| `scala_src/typechecker/FormulaJUTest.scala:177` | the empty solution is a triple now | 1 |

About 213 code lines added in hand-written files (added lines that are neither comment nor blank, modified lines included), against the shadow's re-estimate of about 225 added (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/REPORT.md:605-630`).

## 2. Where the fix belongs

The map's row for `nat` and `int` parameters puts the wall in the checker: `STypesUtil.scala:550-557`, "interp works / comp absent — the wall is the checker, not codegen" (`explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:233`; `:355` in the path table). The checker is the TYPECHECK phase, `compiler/StaticChecker.java` calling the Scala checker (`explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md:266`, `:353`). Code generation already names a size (`NamingCzar.forIntRef`/`forIntBase`, `explorations/perf-probes/nat/java.md:36-38`) and a sized program then fails at load, which is the run-time rung's (`explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:93`). So the fix is in `scala_src/`, and in the one Java class the checker calls on every method invocation, `FnNameInfo.boundsFor`, reached from `scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala:606` and `:730`. Nothing in `compiler/StaticChecker.java`, `runtimeSystem/`, `compiler/runtimeValues/`, `CodeGen.java`, `OverloadSet.java`, `Library/` or `interpreter/` was edited.

## 3. Precedent search

- **Inference variables.** The checker has two, both syntax-tree nodes minted with `new Object()` identity: `_InferenceVarType` (`Fortress.ast:1061`, `NodeFactory.java:1166-1175`) and `_InferenceVarOp` (`Fortress.ast:1593`, `NodeFactory.java:1178-1180`). No inference variable in the tree is a reserved name. The size variable follows them (decision 1).
- **Equality-only constraints.** The operator track is the one whose constraints are equalities (`OPrimitive(pe, ne)`, `Formula.scala:57-61`): its reduce steps `oSimplify`, `oContradiction`, `oTrivial` (`:355-371`), its cliques through `getCliques` and `makeSub` (`:640-642`), its primitive constructors (`:802-806`) and `TypeAnalyzer.pEqv(Op, Op)` (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:342-348`). The size track copies each of these once, with `nEq` in place of `==`. The interpreter's rule is the same three cases (`IntNat.java:126-146`: a literal must be equal, a symbol is bound, anything else fails), which is what the plan ports (`explorations/reviews/nat-checking-plan.md:348-356`).
- **A static argument for a static parameter.** The kind-correct `STypesUtil.staticParamToArg` (`STypesUtil.scala:333-345`) and its list form are called at 17 sites (`grep` of `staticParamsToArgs\|staticParamToArg` over `ProjectFortress/src`, 19 lines less the two definitions). Two sites made a `TypeArg` for every parameter whatever its kind: `AbstractMethodChecker.scala:83` and `FnNameInfo.boundsFor` (`FnNameInfo.java:162-173` before the edit), the Scala and the Java half of one defect (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/REPORT.md:548-580`); both now call the helper. A third helper, `staticParamToArgEnhanced` (`:347-362`), is kind-correct already.
- **The shadow.** `explorations/perf-probes/nat/shadow.patch` built this design in classpath shadows and measured it; `java/java-shadow.patch` the Java site; `size-probes/keep-size-params.patch` the four lines. They are evidence; section 5 lists where the edit differs.
- **The ledger, missed in the first pass.** The search above looked at code, not at the gap ledger, and so missed row 21, "static arguments on a generic *method* cannot be inferred", a walk probe (`explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:135`). The first pass opened a provisional row for the same walk gap (numbered 388 then; withdrawn, and the ledger's row 388 is rung C's) with sizes and `bool` added; the repair round withdraws it and turns it into a note on row 21 (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/record.md`).

## 4. The specification

- **Sizes are part of the language.** "Static parameters may include one or more `nat` and `int` parameters ... These parameters are instantiated at runtime with numeric values. A `nat` parameter may be used to instantiate other `nat` parameters, or to appear in any context that a variable of type ℕ32 can appear" (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:68-90`). The chapter opens with the 2012 draft's note "Non-type static parameters and static expressions are not yet supported" (`:15-17`), which records the implementation of its day.
- **Inference is assumed, not specified.** "We assume throughout this chapter that all static variables in functional calls have been instantiated or inferred" (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex:137-138`); the inference chapter is a placeholder, "This chapter will include the Fortress static type inference mechanism" (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:15`). How an unknown size is treated is therefore governed by Pavol's rule of 09-21 (`explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:47`): an error only when it reaches a type, a name or a value. What "a name" covers on the compiled path is the rung's reading of that rule (decision 3).
- **Arithmetic in a size is in the language.** "Static expressions which use a restricted subset of operations can occur as static arguments" (`Specification/basic/expressions/constant.tex:23-24`, under the draft note "Static expressions are not yet supported", `:15`). Refusing it is a limit of the minimal design that the specification does not share; its test is an expected failure (section 6).
- **`bool`, `dim` and `unit` parameters are in the language** (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:101-120`, `:122-145`). Refusing their inference is a limit; its test is an expected failure.
- **The return-type rule.** "Overloaded declarations must have static parameters that are identical (up to α-equivalence) ... Therefore, static parameters ... are ignored in the remainder of this chapter" (`Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:95-103`), and the Subtype Rule requires the more specific declaration's return type to be a subtype of the other's (`:158-170`); the same sentence in the basic chapter is `Specification/basic/overloading.tex:100-107`, Pavol's open decision (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:33`). The designers' checker implements the rule of their paper instead: `arrow(d1)` must be a subtype of `∀[Δ1, Δ2](S1 ∩ S2) → T2` (`Papers/Types/overloading-check.tick:166-172`), each declaration's static parameters its own. Section 5, decision 2, and section 9 say where the two readings part.

## 5. Decisions, and the deviations from the shadow

**Decision 1: the unknown size is a node, `_InferenceVarInt(Object id)`, not a reserved name.** Pavol left this to the rung (`explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:47`). The alternative is the shadow's `IntRef` named `$nat$k` (option B, `explorations/reviews/nat-checking-plan.md:408-428`).
- For the node: it is the codebase's shape for both its inference variables (section 3), and it removes the four costs the shadow names (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/REPORT.md:122-126`, `:649-655`, `:695-700`): the size cliques go through the tree's own `makeSub`, which splits variables from terms by class (`Formula.scala:646`), instead of a hand-written twin; the constraint map is keyed by the node, not by a string; identity is `new Object()`, not a global counter that is not thread-safe; and no program name can collide with it. The node implements `OutAfterTypeChecking`, like `_InferenceVarType`, so one that survives checking trips the tree's own assertion (`compiler/StaticChecker.java:263-265`, `STypesUtil.scala:1955-1965`) instead of reaching code generation as a symbol.
- Against: the regeneration. Measured: 26 generated files change and 4 are new (`_InferenceVarInt.java`, `TemplateGap_InferenceVarInt.java`, `_Ellipses_InferenceVarInt.java`, `_SyntaxTransformation_InferenceVarInt.java`), 676 inserted lines and no deletion, plus 8 lines in `scala_src/nodes/FortressAst.scala`; `Library/FortressAst.fsi` and `.fss`, which the same target writes, are unchanged (the generator leaves `_`-prefixed nodes out of them). That is the record's bound of about 30 files (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:119`). The regeneration is deterministic: the SHA-256 of the node diff with the four new files was `dcd3bcdb…` after the first regeneration and again after a second one from a touched `Fortress.ast`; no other file changed.

**Decision 2: a size the return-type rule leaves free stays bound, as the less specific declaration's own parameter.** Pavol's rule settles that a free size is no error; the implementation was the rung's (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:129`). Measured on three probe pairs and their type-parameter twins (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/b1-typecheck-probes.txt`, build 1, `keep-size-params` without this decision; `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/typecheck-probes.txt`, the landed edit):

| pair (`probes/`) | the specification | types in the tree (`…T.fss`) | `keep-size-params` alone (build 1) | landed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SubOvUniv`: `Dn.sub[\b,s,o\]: Dn[\T,b,s\]` over `Up.sub: Up[\T,b,s\]`, the library's `subarray` | valid | accepted | accepted | accepted |
| `SubOvOneSize`: `Dn.sub` returns `Dn[\T,3,s\]` | refused | refused (`SubOvOneT`) | **accepted** | refused |
| `SubOvSwap`: `Dn.sub` returns `Dn[\T,s,b\]` | refused | accepted (`SubOvSwapT`) | accepted | accepted |

- With `keep-size-params.patch` alone the free size is an inference variable that leaks into the arrow checked against (`OverloadingOracle.scala:102-106`), where the second inference solves it: the existential reading. It accepts `SubOvOneSize`, which the types' rule refuses and the specification refuses. That is the stop of the batch record (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:127`), so it was not kept.
- The shadow's two-line relaxation in `Formula.imp` reads any residue made only of sizes as satisfied, everywhere the checker asks `lteq`, "a pair whose return types agree for one size only" included (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/followup.md:89-93`): the same acceptance made global. Not taken, and not needed: `keep-size-params.patch` alone already clears the `subarray` refusal the relaxation was written for (the first row above; with `keep-size-params` off, `XXXNatOverrideChecker` gets exactly that error, `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/xxx-goes-red-no-keep.txt:26-31`).
- Taken: `satisfiesReturnTypeRule` keeps each size of the less specific declaration that the domains leave unsolved as that declaration's own static parameter in the arrow it builds (`OverloadingOracle.scala:90-106`), bound as the paper's `σ∧` binds `Δ2` (`Papers/Types/overloading-check.tick:166-172`). Sizes then read exactly as the tree reads type parameters, the third column. Cost: 12 lines, active only when a size escaped (the arrow is untouched otherwise, `:95-97`). `SubOvSwap` stays accepted, as its type twin is today; section 9 says why that is recorded and not stopped on.

**Decision 3: a size left unknown in a call's static arguments is an error at the call** ("Could not infer static argument nat m without context.", `Functionals.scala:246-251`, `ApplicationError.scala:114`). This is the rung's reading of Pavol's rule of 09-21, not the rule itself. The judge kept the reading after the first refusal (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/JUDGE.md` section 4), and it goes to Pavol as the rung's decision.
- **The rule and the reading.** The rule: an unknown size is an error only when it reaches a type, a name or a value, and nothing otherwise (`explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:47`). The rung reads "a name" to cover every static argument of a call, because on the compiled path those arguments name the instantiation the code generator emits (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/java.md:42-45`). The rule's source reads it more narrowly. E2, the option Pavol took, is written as "the interpreter's `BottomType` rule ... the six declarations pass because their dead parameters reach nothing" (`explorations/reviews/array-design-review.md:181`, reasoning at `:81`), and under that rule the interpreter runs a call to a function with a dead size. The specification is silent: the inference chapter is a placeholder (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:15`), and its draft note asks the question for types and leaves it open, "Do we want to forbid such cases where type inference infers BottomTypes for static parameters?" (`:24-25`). The shadow built only the type half (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/REPORT.md:649-655`).
- **(a) Sizes are stricter than types.** A dead type parameter at a call passes, because `killIvars` turns it into `BOTTOM` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/useful/STypesUtil.scala:1937-1940`). A dead size is refused. For a single function: `DeadSize` is refused at both calls (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/typecheck-probes.txt:26-33`), while its type twin `DeadTypeSingle` checks, compiles and prints 3, 7 (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/dead-type-single.txt:2-9`), and walk runs both (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/walk-probes.txt:35-40`, `dead-type-single.txt:10-13`). His question on it was answered by the judgement: the coercions need no rule about identities, since a sum's zero and a product's one carry into every wider type by themselves (measured on both paths), while a maximum's identity is the type's least element and a narrower type's least element is not the wider type's (measured). 13:### Row 379: `walk`'s fixed-width arithmetic wraps silently. Home 2, placed now.
15:**What the specification settles.** `Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:154-155`, read at `:140-176`: "The handling of overflow depends on the type of the number produced. For integer results, overflow throws an `IntegerOverflow`." The same sentence for addition and subtraction at `:195-196`, read at `:190-209`. Wraparound and saturation are given their own spellings, the dotted and boxed operators, at `:172-176` and `:205-209`, and "These operations do not overflow", which is what makes the plain operators the throwing ones. Unary `-` and `|..|` are the negative and the magnitude (`Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:384`, `:624-625`), carried to the fixed widths by `:75-77` ("The other integer types have exactly the same methods"); `-MIN` and `|MIN|` are integer results that do not fit, so `:154-155` reaches them. Measured: `walk` wraps on all twelve cases the row names (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-compiled/probes/skeptic/SkWrapAddSub-walk.txt:2-5`, `probes/skeptic/SkMulGuards-walk.txt:14`, `:29`, `probes/IntSemTableWalk-walk.txt:35-40`), and the compiled path throws on every one (`SkWrapAddSub-compiled.txt:3-6`, `SkMulGuards-compiled.txt:15`, `:30`). The natives are one-line Java arithmetic: `Int$Negate`, `Add`, `Sub`, `Mul`, `Div` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/Int.java:98-126`) and their `Long` twins (`Long.java:112-140`); `|..|` is `if self>=0 then self else -self end` in the library (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:652`, `:710`), so it goes through `Negate`.
17:**Why home 2 and not home 1.** The repair is reserved: the batch record takes "the interpreter's silently wrapping `+`, `-` and multiplication on `ZZ32`/`ZZ64`" out of the batch as "the larger divergence, undecided" (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md:75`), and it is a change of the interpreter's semantics on every fixed-width operation with a cost no one has measured (the 394 files of `testSystem` include hash and random-number code that may rely on wrapping). That is a decision for Pavol, and this ruling does not take it.
19:**Why the gated home is owed anyway.** The shared prefix's second home is for a defect that is deferred *and* settled by the specification; the two conditions are independent, and both hold. Rung B's four reasons (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-compiled/REPORT.md` § 8, the row-379 bullet) do not survive the batch level: "undecided" is about the repair, not the gate; "on rung I's path and corpus" was a rung-scope reason and the review-repair works on the merged tree; "moves the gate's `testSystem` count" is what batch 3's judge answered by placing the tests and running the gate again (`climb-batch-3/JUDGE-review.md` § 2: "`testSystem` goes 389 → 391 and the gate runs again"); and "needs rung I's catchable throw" is satisfied, `Int.overflow()` landed (`Int.java:256-259`). "Row 347 set the precedent" is not a precedent: row 347's sentence was itself written at climb batch 2's gather to correct rung W's omission of the same home (`explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md:71`), before the three-homes rule was in the prefix. The `XXX` file asserts the specification's answer and prejudges nothing: if Pavol decides `walk` keeps wrapping, that is "any change of semantics against the spec" (`explorations/coordinator/PLAN.md:52`), a fork, and the file leaves with the decision; until then it turns the suite red the day someone makes the ten natives throw without closing the row.
21:**The test.** `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXFixedWidthOverflowRungB.fss`, an interpreter expected-failure test (FACTS `:71`: `FileTests.java:710-711` hands `s.startsWith("XXX")` to `SourceFileTest` as `shouldFail`; a run that passes reaches `:400-402`, "Missing expected failure"). It asserts a catchable `IntegerOverflow` on the row's twelve cases, `+`, `-`, unary `-`, `|..|`, `DIV` and `DOT` on both widths, through the `overflows` helper of `ProjectFortress/tests/IntSemanticsRungI.fss:6-12`. Two decisions: one file for the row, not one per operator, because the row closes as one and a partial repair leaves the row open and the file an expected failure, which is the truthful state; and the twelve cases rather than two, so that the deliberate fix that shows it red must cover every native the row names, which is what a real repair does. Shown red on that fix, ten natives edited and reverted (§ 4, steps 7-8). content.content:
### Serious 5. The census "no arithmetic occurs inside white brackets anywhere in the library" is false for the three storing objects the array rungs need

The claim (§6c): "Every one of these is a symbol or a literal; no arithmetic occurs inside white brackets anywhere in the library or in the two microGPT programs … So the minimal checker, symbols and literals unified by equality, covers all 81". The nat plan's census (`nat-checking-plan.md` §d) counted "an operator inside white brackets" and found 0.

The tree. `object __DefaultArray2 … mem:PrimitiveArray[\T, (s0 s1) \]` (`FortressLibrary.fss:2420`), `__DefaultMatrix` the same (`:2568`), `__DefaultArray3 … mem:PrimitiveArray[\T,(s0 (s1 s2))\]` (`:2785`). Juxtaposition is multiplication in a static argument: the interpreter evaluates it as `IntBinaryOp` with the operator `" "` (`EvalType.java:461`), and the compiler's mangler spells it `IntBinaryOp` too (`NamingCzar.java:1899-1904`). The plan's `TypeWellFormedChecker` rule rejects any `IntArg` containing `IntBinaryOp` (`nat-checking-plan.md` §c, "What it touches"), so the minimal checker refuses the library's own rank-2 and rank-3 storage. `NatReflect.fss:42-46` (`__refl'[\r+b, b+b\]`) is the fourth site and the design admits that one (§6d).

What follows. Option (c)'s storing objects are rewritten, not copied: a store trait that carries its size as a run-time field instead of `PrimitiveArray[\T,(s0 s1)\]` in the type is what §6d's "the field first" amounts to. That is a departure from the library's text and it is not named as one. The alternative, static arithmetic in the checker, is what the specification marks "not yet supported" (`basic/expressions/constant.tex:15`) and what the team's meeting refused for overloading (`internal-document.tex:167-182`); it is a decision, not a default.

### Serious 6. The array rung of §8 hides three pieces of `.java` work, so the count of gated batches is at least three, not two

Every overloading error is a pair of declarations that the checker cannot separate: neither is more specific, their domains do not exclude, and no declaration sits on their meet (the Subtype Rule and the Meet Rule, `Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:149-166`, `:224-260`). content.content:
\seclabel{basic-integers}

The trait \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} (\STR{ZZ}) encompasses all finite integers,
the results of starting from \EXP{0} and repeatedly adding or subtracting \EXP{1} a finite number of times.

\Library\ also declare four integer types of fixed size.
The five integer types are these:

\begin{tabbing}
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}} (\STR{ZZ}) is the set of integers (it coerces from \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}64}, and \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}).
\\
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} (\STR{ZZ64}) is the set of integers representable in 64-bit two's-complement form (it coerces from \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} and \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}).
\\
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} (\STR{ZZ32}) is the set of integers representable in 32-bit two's-complement form.
\\
\EXP{\mathbb{N}64} (\STR{NN64}) is the set of integers representable in 64-bit unsigned binary form (it coerces from \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}).
\\
\EXP{\mathbb{N}32} (\STR{NN32}) is the set of integers representable in 32-bit unsigned binary form.
\end{tabbing}

Like every number type, each of them is a subtype of \TYP{Number} and of no other
number type (\secref{basic-rationals}), and each coerces into \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}.
An integer type coerces from each other integer type all of whose values it holds,
as listed above; every other conversion between integer types is written explicitly.

It is often desirable to know that an integer lies in a subset of its type,
such as the positive values or the nonzero values.
As for the rationals, such subsets are not types of their own:
a program tests an integer's sign at run time with the comparison operators.
The integer types hold no infinite value.

Here we present only the trait \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} and its methods.
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}} is a commutative ring and is totally ordered.
%% For the exact details of how all this is implemented,
%% \see{advanced-integers}.
\emph{Future versions of this specification will include
the exact details of how all this is implemented.}
\revision{revival-numbers}{The Working Draft of February 2011 gave the integers
twelve types, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, the type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}^*} that adds the two
infinities, and five refinements of each by sign, each a subtype of the
